boards.title: Your First Weekend at California State University-Sacramento, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence connecting Sac State orientation points, campus art and reflection spaces, Midtown, civic landmarks, and riverside recreation.

cards.title: Friday: Get Oriented at the Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: Start with the official campus map and self-guided options
cards.notes: Open the searchable campus map at the Welcome Center, mark the weekend stops, and check parking signs before exploring on foot.
cards.short_summary: Establish a campus reference point before the weekend begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State tours begin and end at the Welcome Center, while the official campus map identifies buildings, parking, bike information, and landmarks.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided materials are referenced by the university. Campus parking requires a permit and is enforced continuously.

cards.title: Friday: Walk the University Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Follow the three-acre garden’s self-guided trail
cards.notes: Walk slowly through the labeled collection and photograph one unfamiliar tree or flowering plant to identify after the visit.
cards.short_summary: Meet the campus through its living botanical collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Arboretum is a three-acre botanic garden with about 1,400 plant species and descriptive trail signage intended for self-guided visits.
cards.access_notes: The source describes casual self-guided visits but does not publish current daily access hours; check campus conditions before going.

cards.title: Friday: See What Is Showing at the Library Gallery
cards.subtitle: Use the academic-year gallery window before the weekend
cards.notes: Enter before the posted closing time, read the exhibition text first, then choose one work to discuss with a new classmate.
cards.short_summary: Add a focused art stop to the first afternoon on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento State’s University Galleries include the University Library Gallery, which is open Tuesday through Friday from noon to 4 p.m. during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Visit Friday between noon and 4 p.m. during the academic year; the galleries close for campus holidays and summer months.

cards.title: Friday: Reset in the Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Take a quiet fifteen-minute pause in the North Lounge
cards.notes: Silence electronics, leave food outside, and use the room briefly for reflection before transitioning into the off-campus weekend.
cards.short_summary: Create a deliberate pause after the first campus circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Union Meditation Room is on the second floor in the North Lounge, is accessible to everyone, and is free to use with a requested 15-minute limit.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are 7 a.m.–5:30 p.m. Monday through Friday; it is closed Saturday and Sunday. Observe the 15-minute limit.

cards.title: Saturday: Browse the Midtown Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Begin downtown at 20th and K streets
cards.notes: Walk the full market footprint, note which vendors grow or make their products regionally, and treat purchases as optional.
cards.short_summary: Use a recurring Saturday market to encounter Sacramento producers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Midtown Association operates the market every Saturday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at 1050 20th Street, with regional produce, prepared food, crafts, and live music.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are Saturday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. Vendor purchases are optional; consult the market page for weekly programming.

cards.title: Saturday: Circle McKinley Park
cards.subtitle: Pair the jogging path with the rose garden and pond
cards.notes: Follow one circuit of the mapped jogging path, pause at the rose garden, and use only designated pedestrian areas.
cards.short_summary: Shift from Midtown activity to a mapped neighborhood green space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Sacramento’s official McKinley Park map identifies a jogging path, rose garden, lake, tennis courts, picnic areas, and restrooms at 3330 McKinley Boulevard.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor amenities are mapped by the city. Organized use and reservations may carry fees; follow posted park rules and closures.

cards.title: Saturday: Read the Memorials in Capitol Park
cards.subtitle: Explore the grounds while the Capitol building is closed
cards.notes: Stay outdoors, locate two named memorials on the grounds, and read their inscriptions rather than expecting a weekend building tour.
cards.short_summary: Approach California civic history through the Capitol grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: California State Parks places the Capitol Museum and Capitol Park at 10th and L streets and identifies memorials on the grounds; the Capitol building is closed on weekends.
cards.access_notes: The Capitol building and guided tours are closed on weekends. This stop is limited to accessible outdoor park areas; construction may alter access.

cards.title: Saturday: Walk Old Sacramento’s Historic Core
cards.subtitle: Finish downtown among preserved and reconstructed sites
cards.notes: Begin near the Passenger Station, compare an original structure with a reconstruction, and keep museum admission separate from the walk.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday with a self-paced look at the historic district.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Sacramento State Historic Park forms part of a National Historic Landmark district and contains original and reconstructed buildings, including the Passenger Station and B.F. Hastings Building.
cards.source_title: Accessible Features at California State Railroad Museum POI
cards.access_notes: Outdoor district access and individual building hours differ. Museums, tours, parking, and concessions may require payment.

cards.title: Sunday: Follow the American River Trail
cards.subtitle: Use the Guy West Bridge area as the campus-side approach
cards.notes: Choose a short out-and-back walk, stay left on the soft shoulder, and step completely off the trail whenever you stop.
cards.short_summary: Reconnect the campus edge with the American River Parkway.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacramento County identifies the 32-mile Jedediah Smith Memorial Trail as a route for walking, jogging, cycling, and skating, open year-round from sunrise to sunset.
cards.source_title: American River Parkway - Jedediah Smith Memorial Trail
cards.access_notes: Open sunrise to sunset. Walkers should use the left soft shoulder; parking at county access points carries a posted vehicle fee.

cards.title: Sunday: Close the Weekend at The WELL
cards.subtitle: Use the recreation membership attached to enrollment
cards.notes: Bring a valid credential, check the day’s informal-recreation schedule, and choose an included activity before setting up the week.
cards.short_summary: End with a practical introduction to student recreation resources.
cards.evidence_claim: All Sacramento State students are eligible for WELL membership through mandatory semester student fees, with access to most programs and services at no additional charge.
cards.access_notes: Student membership dates track enrollment terms. Verify current building and informal-recreation hours, present required credentials, and note that some programs cost extra.
